title.value: Amortized Rejection Sampling in Universal Probabilistic Programming
title.justification: The title is directly taken from the cover page and repeated in the header of the paper's pages, clearly indicating the main topic of the research.
title.quote: Amortized Rejection Sampling in Universal Probabilistic Programming

analysis.description: The paper introduces a new method for amortized importance sampling in universal probabilistic programming languages, specifically targeting the issue of infinite variance in estimators caused by naive inference approaches in programs with rejection sampling loops. The paper presents both theoretical proofs and empirical demonstrations of the proposed method’s effectiveness.

type.justification: The paper includes empirical demonstrations and comparisons of the proposed method against existing alternatives, indicating an empirical nature.
type.quote: We prove finite variance of our estimator and empirically demonstrate our method’s correctness and efficiency compared to existing alternatives on generative programs containing rejection sampling loops.

name.justification: The research primarily focuses on improving inference methods within probabilistic programming frameworks, a subfield of machine learning dealing with models that utilize probability distributions to express uncertainty.
name.quote: It is now understood how to apply probabilistic programming inference techniques to generative models written in “universal” probabilistic programming languages (PPLs).

name.justification: The paper deals with issues related to sampling methods, specifically rejection sampling and importance sampling, which are important techniques in machine learning for probabilistic inference.
name.quote: The specific problem we address, that of efficient amortized importance-sampling-based inference in models with user-defined rejection sampling loops...

name.justification: Inference Compilation is referenced as a method being examined and built upon in the paper, as well as being compared against the new estimator introduced in the paper.
name.quote: This paper examines and builds on the latter “Inference Compilation” (IC) approach.

is_contributed.justification: The paper does not introduce Inference Compilation but rather uses it as a baseline for comparisons.
is_contributed.quote: This paper examines and builds on the latter “Inference Compilation” (IC) approach.

referenced_paper_title.quote: Mini-SHERPA, however, has up to 11 latent variables... Its naming comes from SHERPA (Gleisberg et al., 2009), the state-of-the-art simulator of high-energy reactions of particles.
